findings.description: Long-term AWS credentials (access_key and secret_key) are embedded in cleartext in the Lambda environment variables block and committed to version control. Anyone with repository access, Terraform state access, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration permission can retrieve them and authenticate as the associated IAM principal; the function should rely solely on its execution role instead.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables — which contain secrets — are protected only by the AWS-managed default key and are returned in cleartext by GetFunctionConfiguration and shown in the console to any principal with read access, with no separate key-policy authorisation gate.

The function uses nodejs12.x, which has reached end of support and no longer receives security patches for the runtime or its bundled libraries, leaving any discovered vulnerability permanently unpatched.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes in the AWS-managed network with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or NACL boundary, providing an unmonitored exfiltration path for the credentials held in its environment.

No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so the deployment package is not cryptographically validated before execution and a tampered or substituted zip artifact would be accepted and run by the function.
